## [Transportation Networks Design](https://github.com/fqueyroi/tulip_plugins/tree/master/TransportationNetworks)

Directory "TransportationNetworks" contains two transportation network construction algorithms. 
- SPRouting: use iterative shortest-path routing of flow
- PhysariumSolver: use biologically inspired routing and edge length update.

### [Cliques](https://github.com/fqueyroi/tulip_plugins/tree/master/Cliques)

A plugin to enumerate all [maximal cliques](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clique_(graph_theory)) in the graph.
metadata.reason: Names a plugin that enumerates all maximal cliques in a graph.

metadata.value: the algorithm of Eppstein et al. (https://arxiv.org/abs/1006.5440)
metadata.normalized_value: the algorithm of Eppstein et al. (https://arxiv.org/abs/1006.5440)
metadata.evidence: It uses [the algorithm of Eppstein *et al.*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1006.5440) : vertices are ordered using their degeneracy value (the [K-Cores plugin](https://github.com/Tulip-Dev/tulip/blob/master/plugins/metric/KCores.cpp) in Tulip) in order to speed up the enumeration.
metadata.reason: Identifies the underlying maximal clique enumeration algorithm and its arXiv reference, plus the degeneracy ordering optimization.

metadata.reason: Installation requirement for the Cliques plugin on Python versions prior to 2.7.

metadata.evidence:
### [Clique Percolation](https://github.com/fqueyroi/tulip_plugins/tree/master/Cliques)

An implementation of the [Clique Percolation Method](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clique_percolation_method) that finds an overlapping clustering of the graph. It does so by merging the k-cliques that share k-1 vertices (k is a parameter of the algorithm). We actually use the plugin `CliqueEnum` to find maximal cliques rather than enumerating all $k$-cliques.
metadata.reason: Names a plugin implementing the Clique Percolation Method for overlapping clustering, including its parameter k and dependency on the CliqueEnum plugin.

### [Label Propagation](https://github.com/fqueyroi/tulip_plugins/tree/master/LabelPropagation)

A simple, fast and efficient graph clustering algorithm. For a weighted graph G=(V,E,w), it produces a *partition* of the vertices V.
metadata.reason: Names a graph clustering plugin that partitions vertices of a weighted graph via label propagation.

metadata.value: the problem is to find a Vertex Cycle Cover of G. This problem can be solved using a maximum matching algorithm.
metadata.normalized_value: the problem is to find a Vertex Cycle Cover of G. This problem can be solved using a maximum matching algorithm.
metadata.evidence: If we assume the the various possibilities are summed up in a graph G (an arc between A->B indicates that A can offer a gift to B) then the problem is to find a [Vertex Cycle Cover](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vertex_cycle_cover) of G. This problem can be solved using a maximum matching algorithm.
metadata.reason: Describes the algorithmic approach (vertex cycle cover via maximum matching) used by the Secret Santa plugin.

metadata.evidence: This is an implementation of the algorithm by [Liberti and Raimondi](https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-540-68880-8_26) (2008).
metadata.reason: Identifies the published algorithm implemented by the SecretSanta plugin for secrecy-preserving assignments.
